transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-12-18
Start time: 16:00 PST
Duration: ~52 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Diego Alvarez (Redwood SE), Rina Patel (Cypress Head of Search), Marcus Lee (Cypress SRE), Anya V. (Cypress ML)

Summary:
Quick hosted API demo focused on embeddings + reranking for product search. Walked through Redwood Console relevance tuning suggestions and Optimize recommendations for batching/quantization. Discussed security requirements (SOC 2, KMS), latency SLOs, and next steps for a Jan POC benchmark.

Topics covered:
- Current stack and pain points (Elastic + Redis caching + Pinecone for vectors)
- Redwood hosted embeddings endpoint and reranker endpoint flow
- Console: per-route latency/cost breakdown, trace hooks, prompt sets for evals
- Optimize suggestions: batching, prefix caching, quantization tradeoffs
- Security: SOC 2, KMS, VPC options and private deployments

Transcript:
[00:00] Maya Chen: Hey everyone thanks for jumping on, can you hear me ok?
[00:04] Rina Patel: Yeah, loud and clear. Thanks Maya.
[00:06] Marcus Lee: yep, good here.
[00:08] Maya Chen: Awesome. Quick intros, I'm Maya at Redwood, Diego is our SE, and from Cypress?
[00:12] Rina Patel: Rina, head of search. We own the relevance work.
[00:14] Marcus Lee: Marcus, SRE. I'm mostly here for perf and networking.
[00:16] Anya V.: Anya, ML eng, focusing on embeddings and rerank.
[00:20] Maya Chen: Great. Real quick, goal for today is to show how our hosted API handles embeddings plus a rerank step, and how the Console and Optimize suggestions help lower cost while meeting latency SLOs. Does that match expectations?
[00:28] Rina Patel: Yeah, also want to see how easy the POC would be and what security paperwork we need.
[00:31] Maya Chen: Perfect. Diego will start with the API demo and then I'll flip into Console.

[00:45] Diego Alvarez: Ok sharing screen. I'll run a small end-to-end: we index sample docs, call embeddings endpoint to vectorize queries, do a vector search, then call our reranker endpoint to get a final ordered score.
[00:55] Anya V.: Are you using dense retrieval or hybrid?
[00:57] Diego Alvarez: For the demo it's dense + a small lexical filter. The reranker is an optional second call to Redwood that takes the top K candidates and finalizes order.
[01:12] Marcus Lee: Quick question on latency budget. Our SLO target for product search is p95 under 150 ms. Does hosted include the rerank roundtrip within that?
[01:20] Diego Alvarez: It depends on settings. If you use a single model for both embedding and rerank with small K and enable continuous batching, you can hit <150ms in many cases. But for heavy rerank models with long context it can be higher. We also have a low-latency rerank variant that trades some quality for speed.
[01:36] Rina Patel: How do we measure cost? Per call? Per token?
[01:39] Diego Alvarez: Embeddings are per vector unit, rerank is per-token. Our Console shows a token-level cost breakdown per route so you can see cost impact of changing K or model.

[02:05] Maya Chen: I'll show the Console realtime dashboards. Here is per-route latency, token consumption, and also our Optimize tab which suggests batching parameters and quant profiles based on historical traces.
[02:18] Rina Patel: Nice, so it actually recommends batch sizes?
[02:20] Maya Chen: Yes, it recommends batching thresholds and caching strategies like prefix caching and KV cache warmup windows. For example, for your product pages with many repeated prefixes, enabling prefix caching reduces token work by ~25% in similar customers.
[02:36] Anya V.: That sounds promising. Can we tune rerank only on a subset of traffic? Like canary?
[02:40] Diego Alvarez: Absolutely. We support canary rollouts and A/B splits at route-level. You can route by header, cookie, or a sampling percentage. We also surface quality deltas on your evals.

[03:05] Marcus Lee: Security real quick — we need SOC 2, SSO, and customer-managed KMS. Does Redwood hosted support KMS?
[03:12] Maya Chen: Hosted supports customer KMS integration via our key wrapping flow and we have SOC 2 Type II. For stricter requirements we have Redwood Private which runs in your VPC or on-prem. We'll send the SOC 2 report and the KMS whitepaper after the call.
[03:30] Rina Patel: Good. Also data residency — some EU traffic must stay in EU. Can we pin regions?
[03:35] Diego Alvarez: Yes, region pinning and routing policies are supported, with fallbacks to compatible model variants.

[03:50] Anya V.: Can you show the rerank request/response schema?
[03:54] Diego Alvarez: Sure. Rerank takes a list of candidate doc snippets plus the query and returns scores and optional highlight spans. For the demo I'll show a small python snippet calling the /v1/rerank endpoint.
[04:10] Diego Alvarez: Running now. Example: request has fields candidates, query, metadata, and we pass model: redwood-ranker-small.
[04:20] Diego Alvarez: You can also pass eval_id to tie calls to a specific prompt set for quality tracking.
[04:27] Rina Patel: Do you store the full request text or are there retention controls?
[04:31] Maya Chen: By default we retain logs for 30 days for hosted; enterprise and private have configurable retention and can disable request body retention. All access is logged.

[04:50] Marcus Lee: Network egress — for us if we use hosted, can we restrict IP egress or need VPC peering?
[04:54] Diego Alvarez: For hosted customer facing, you get public endpoints. If you need private networking we recommend Redwood Private with a VPC connector. For the POC many customers do a short-term public route with secure token and client side IP restrictions.

[05:20] Maya Chen: Switching to Optimize. This is where we suggest quantization variants per model class. For example we might suggest int8 quant for embeddings host to cut GPU memory and cost with minimal quality loss.
[05:35] Anya V.: How do you validate quality after quant?
[05:38] Diego Alvarez: We run a small prompt set of your queries through candidate models and compute MRR and nDCG deltas. Console shows a regression threshold and will alert if quality drops beyond your threshold.

[06:05] Rina Patel: Ok show us a live relevance test with our sample dataset. We gave you 5k labeled cases earlier?
[06:11] Diego Alvarez: We have a small subset. I'm going to trigger a rerank on 100 queries and show the eval comparison between model variants.
[06:20] Diego Alvarez: Running batch eval now. Note there may be some delay — this is running against our hosted eval infra.
[06:45] [silence while eval runs]
[07:02] Diego Alvarez: Results coming in. Model A baseline MRR 0.68, Model B quantized MRR 0.66, but Model B saves ~30% cost. Console flags the delta and suggests if that's acceptable given your SLO.
[07:18] Rina Patel: We usually target MRR > 0.67 so that quantized model might be borderline. Can we do per-route model selection?
[07:24] Maya Chen: Yes you can route expensive model only for high value queries and fall back to cheaper model for bulk traffic. That routing policy is configurable in the Console.

[07:48] Marcus Lee: For the POC we want to run 1M queries of a production-like mix to measure p95 and cost. How long to spin up a POC?
[07:56] Maya Chen: For hosted POC we can start within days. We'll need sample logs and a test harness. Diego will provide an infra checklist and we'll coordinate on region.

[08:12] Anya V.: How does prefix caching interact with rerank?
[08:16] Diego Alvarez: Prefix caching helps embeddings and autoregressive models by caching tokenized prefixes in the KV cache. For rerank, if your candidates share a lot of context we can also cache candidate encodings. It's called candidate KV warmup in our UI.

[08:38] Rina Patel: Competitors question — we've been evaluating Pinecone plus a hosted LLM for rerank. How is Redwood different?
[08:45] Maya Chen: Pinecone is great as a vector DB. Redwood combines the hosting of the model runtime and the operational controls — so you get rerank as a single API call with instrumentation, cost telemetry and routing policies. It reduces glue code and gives you builtin evals and Optimize suggestions.

[09:10] Marcus Lee: Latency vs cost tradeoff — if we go dedicated what gains?
[09:14] Diego Alvarez: Dedicated GPUs give predictable throughput and lower p95 variance. For high qps and tight latency SLOs we often recommend Dedicated capacity. There's also reserved capacity pricing.

[09:30] Rina Patel: Any guardrails on hallucination or biased rerank output?
[09:33] Diego Alvarez: Our rerank models are discriminative and score candidates; hallucination risk is lower than generation tasks. We also let you attach validation checks in the pipeline and produce traces to aid debugging.

[09:52] Maya Chen: Ok quick demo of the API call flow. I'll show a python snippet for embeddings then rerank.
[09:58] Maya Chen: code sample: embeddings = client.embeddings.create(model='redwood-embed-1', input=query) then search topK in vector DB then rerank = client.rerank.create(model='redwood-ranker-small', candidates=topk, query=query).
[10:20] Anya V.: Does rerank accept metadata signals? click-through data?
[10:24] Diego Alvarez: Yes you can pass per-candidate metadata and we can include that as features. We also support offline reweighting via our Optimize export.

[10:40] Rina Patel: For the POC what production counters do you collect?
[10:44] Maya Chen: Token counts, per-route latency histograms, error rates, cold-start counts, cache hit rates, and model quality deltas tied to eval prompt sets. You can export these to your observability stack.

[11:05] Marcus Lee: Any limits on request size for rerank? We sometimes send 50 candidate snippets.
[11:10] Diego Alvarez: We recommend keeping K to 20-50; beyond that the cost and latency scale. For large K we suggest doing a first-pass coarse filter or using compressed candidate representations.

[11:30] Rina Patel: Anything special for relevance tuning?
[11:33] Diego Alvarez: Use small curated prompt sets representing failure cases. Console's Eval feature will show per-slice metrics, so you can tune on queries that matter most.

[12:02] Maya Chen: Alright let's switch to pricing briefly. Our hosted pricing is usage-based. Embeddings per vector unit and rerank per token. For the POC we can give a trial credit and custom rate for expected scale.
[12:18] Rina Patel: We'll want an estimate for 1M queries with K=10 rerank.
[12:21] Maya Chen: We'll run numbers and share an estimate — Diego will include cost sensitivity to K and model size.

[12:35] Anya V.: Quick nit: we have a regulatory constraint, logs containing PII must be redacted before transmission. Can that be enforced?
[12:41] Diego Alvarez: You can redact client side and we offer request body redaction at intake in enterprise/private modes. We'll include that in the security docs.

[13:00] Rina Patel: For the eval run you did earlier, can we get the raw outputs and the candidate scores?
[13:04] Diego Alvarez: Yes, we can export eval results and the trace IDs per request.

[13:20] Marcus Lee: About SLA — do you offer uptime SLAs for hosted?
[13:24] Maya Chen: We have SLA-backed tiers for Dedicated customers. Hosted has high availability but we typically recommend Dedicated for strict enterprise SLAs.

[13:40] Rina Patel: Let's talk resourcing internally — who should own the POC from your side?
[13:44] Maya Chen: I'll be the AE lead; Diego will be the technical lead during the POC. We'll also have Solutions Eng available for benchmarks.

[13:58] Anya V.: Any recommended metrics we should measure during the POC?
[14:01] Diego Alvarez: p95 latency, MRR/nDCG on labeled set, cost per 1k queries, cache hit rate, and cold-start frequency.

[14:20] Maya Chen: Closing demo notes. We'll send an agenda for the POC and an infra checklist.
[14:26] Rina Patel: Sounds good. A couple of quick follow-ups: can we get a whitepaper on quantization effects and a sample of how routing policies are configured?
[14:33] Maya Chen: Yes to both. Diego will attach sample routing policy yaml and a short whitepaper.

[14:50] Diego Alvarez: Anything else from Cypress side?
[14:53] Marcus Lee: Not from me. We'll sync internally and get samples to you.
[14:57] Rina Patel: We'll aim to have sample logs and acceptance criteria by Friday 2026-12-21.

[15:05] Maya Chen: Great. Recap of next steps and owners are in the action items. We'll follow up with scheduling the Jan benchmark. Thanks all.
[15:12] All: Thanks!

Notes: Transcript contains minor transcription errors in proper nouns and some technical terms (e.g., K-V cache sometimes transcribed as K-V cash, VP-C instead of VPC).
